subject: Political Science
central_question: How did coalition politics, caste-based representation, religious mobilisation, economic reform and a new policy consensus reshape Indian politics after 1989?
in_scope_units: Context of the 1990s: five developments that transformed national politics.
Era of Coalitions: decline of Congress dominance and rise of multi-party governments.
Alliance politics: National Front, United Front, NDA and UPA arrangements.
Political Rise of Other Backward Classes: Mandal politics and new representation.
The Mandal Commission: purpose, recommendations, implementation and judicial review.
Political fallouts: BAMCEF, BSP and Dalit–Bahujan mobilisation.
Communalism, Secularism, Democracy: rise of BJP, Hindutva and the Shah Bano controversy.
Ayodhya issue: legal, political and constitutional resolution.
Emergence of a new consensus: elections from 2004 to 2019 and broad areas of agreement.
Growing consensus: economic policy, backward caste claims, regional parties and pragmatic alliances.
banned_topics: Detailed case studies of Narmada Bachao Andolan, Chipko or farmers’ movements, because they are not present in the supplied chapter text.
Detailed analysis of the 1975 Emergency, which belongs to an earlier chapter.
Regional autonomy conflicts in Punjab, Assam, Mizoram and Kashmir, which belong to the chapter on Regional Aspirations.

known_pitfalls.claim: The 1989 election immediately replaced Congress dominance with another single-party dominant system.
known_pitfalls.correction: No single party replaced Congress; the result began a multi-party and coalition era in which regional parties became crucial.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Mandal Commission dealt only with electoral reservations.
known_pitfalls.correction: It investigated social and educational backwardness and recommended measures including reservation in education and government employment, as well as reforms such as land reform.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coalition politics ended completely after the BJP won majorities in 2014 and 2019.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says the trend changed, but coalition recognition remained relevant and the BJP still formed NDA governments with partners.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 3 to identify the main issues in politics after 1989.
Use NCERT Exercise 4 to evaluate whether coalitions were based less on ideology and more on power sharing.
Use NCERT Exercise 5 to trace the rise of BJP after the Emergency.
Use NCERT Exercise 6 to assess the continuing influence of Congress despite decline.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to analyse the challenge of accommodating and aggregating diverse interests.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The supplied chapter ends with an EXERCISES section containing Questions 1–8, followed by a LET US DO IT TOGETHER activity.
